userStories.title: S0.3a — The socials service: status machine, content hash, approval and the publish guard
userStories.description: modules/socials/service.py owns the post lifecycle as pure, tested logic. (a) The status machine: an explicit allowed-transitions table over the D2 statuses; an illegal transition raises IllegalTransition. Wave 0 transitions: draft -> needs_approval (submit); changes_requested -> needs_approval (submit); needs_approval -> approved | changes_requested | archived (reject); approved -> scheduled (schedule) -> approved (unschedule); approved|scheduled -> needs_approval (any content edit). Rendering, publishing, missed and failed transitions arrive with their waves. (b) compute_content_hash(post): sha256 over canonical JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False) of copy, variables, sources, format, template_id and media. Docstring: Wave 1 extends 'media' with the rendered files' digests. (c) create_draft, update_post (recomputes the hash; if an approved or scheduled post's hash changes, status -> needs_approval and the approval is void because approved_hash != content_hash), submit, approve(user, override_unsourced=False), request_changes(user, comment), reject(user, reason), schedule(scheduled_for, timezone), unschedule. Every review action appends to review_log. (d) D7: unsourced_claims(post) returns the names of variables with claim=true that have no entry in sources. approve raises UnsourcedClaims(names) unless override_unsourced=True, in which case override_unsourced is stored and the review_log entry names the claims. (e) assert_publishable(post) raises NotPublishable unless status is approved or scheduled AND approved_hash == content_hash. (f) modules/socials/publisher.py: publish_post(db, post) calls assert_publishable FIRST, then — Wave 0 has no channel publishers — raises PublishingUnavailable. This is the seam S3.3 fills; nothing in it calls Composio yet.

userStories.title: S0.3b — The /api/socials routes behind the gate

Mount it the way other routers are mounted (grep main.py's include_router list). Every route depends on require_socials_enabled (US-001) and on the caller's workspace; every query filters by that workspace_id, so another workspace's post is a 404. approve additionally requires 'socials:approve' (403 otherwise). userStories.title: [HIGH] The Composio deny list fails OPEN when its settings read errors
userStories.description: core/composio/deny_list.py:73 reads composio.denied_actions through core.llm.manager.get_system_setting, which catches EVERY exception (core/llm/manager.py:93-96), logs it at DEBUG and returns the default — None here. parse_denied_actions(None) (deny_list.py:57-58) means 'nothing denied'. So any failed read lets HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CONFIRM_BILLING_PURCHASE (and every other D16 slug) execute, silently: pool exhaustion or timeout on the ad-hoc SessionLocal the helper opens on every call (up to three per execution: tool_executor.py twice, client.py once), a dropped connection or a statement timeout. Verified: the real get_system_setting and composio_action_denial bodies, with SessionLocal raising, return None for HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CONFIRM_BILLING_PURCHASE. This contradicts the module's own contract ('a guard on real money fails closed') and the platform rule at main.py:894 ('A gate that can't decide must deny'). Keep 'no row, or an empty value → nothing denied' (a stack without the seed). Only a read that could not complete must refuse.

userStories.description: api/socials.py writes every lifecycle change except approve as load → mutate → commit, with no check that the row is still what the request loaded: PATCH (:231-248), submit (:256-267), request-changes (:298-310), reject (:313-326), schedule (:329-341) and unschedule (:344-355). SQLAlchemy's UPDATE carries only the columns the request dirtied. service._log (modules/socials/service.py:307-315) reassigns the whole review_log list, so the last writer's stale copy wins. service.update_post (:382-404) decides whether to void an approval from the status it LOADED. Reproduced in-process with the real router over SQLite, using the RVW-2 harness (a second session commits between the route's load and its commit): (1) A PATCH that loaded the post in needs_approval before an approve committed answers 200. The committed row is status=approved, approved_by=the reviewer, copy = the edit nobody reviewed, approved_hash ≠ content_hash, and review_log is [submit, approve] with no approval_voided. (2) A schedule that loaded before a PATCH committed answers 200. The row is status=scheduled on the edited copy, approved_hash ≠ content_hash, and the PATCH's approval_voided entry is gone (review_log [submit, approve, schedule]). (3) An unschedule that loaded before a PATCH committed leaves status=approved on the edited copy, and approval_voided is gone. (4) A PATCH adding variables {users: {value, claim: true}} while an approve committed leaves status=approved with an unsourced claim, override_unsourced=false, and nothing about the claim in review_log (D7). assert_publishable (service.py:500-509) recomputes the hash and refuses all four, so nothing unapproved can be published. But D6 ('Any edit resets approval ... moves the post back to needs_approval') and D7 do not hold in the stored state. The tab shows Approved or Scheduled, and the history the approval UI shows loses entries. P251-RVW-2 closed only the approve side: its notes put request-changes and reject out of scope. The 3ddc55a02 body flagged this mirror race, but no story covers it.
